title: What $\chi(\mathcal{S})=-6$ fixes about the Reeb bundle, and what it does not
html: What the theorem says. The Euler characteristic \chi(\mathcal{S}) = -6 of Bring's surface fixes the topology of the Reeb bundle \xi: its Euler class is -6, so \xi has no nowhere-vanishing section, and \xi has an n-th root exactly for n \in \{1, 2, 3, 6\}. These are statements about the global class on the surface \mathcal{S}. On any one-dimensional locus \Sigma every such class restricts to zero, so the theorem gives no obstruction on a vortex-collision curve and no statement about blow-up of a flow.
